highlight.title: GCSE & A-Level Formula Sheets Continue Through 2027
highlight.summary: Students won't need to memorise formulae for maths, physics and combined science GCSEs in 2026-2027, with sheets provided in exam papers. This decision supports those whose education was disrupted and helps students with special educational needs focus on application rather than memorisation.

resources.title: BBC Bitesize GCSE & A-Level Revision App
resources.why_now: Perfect for students preparing for May-June 2026 exams with flashcards, quizzes and exam board-specific content across all major GCSE subjects.

resources.title: Oak National Academy KS3 & KS4 Curriculum Resources
resources.why_now: Ideal for both students and parents as Oak provides free, structured lesson resources for Years 7-11 plus their new AI lesson assistant Aila for personalised study support.

resources.title: Ofqual Student Guide to 2026 Exams
resources.why_now: Essential reading for parents to understand key exam dates (7 May - 23 June 2026), access arrangements, and contingency planning for GCSE and A-Level students.

resources.title: KS3 SATs Past Papers & Revision Materials
resources.why_now: Valuable for Year 8-9 students and parents as many schools use internal assessments based on these formats, plus free access to 25+ years of papers with mark schemes.

claude_take: The continuation of formula sheets through 2027 is excellent news for reducing exam anxiety and allowing students to focus on understanding rather than rote memorisation. Parents should take advantage of the wealth of free UK government resources like Oak National Academy and BBC Bitesize rather than expensive alternatives - these are specifically designed for the UK curriculum and regularly updated.
